question: Should Discord Activity support continue from this stale branch, move to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/65205, or restart as a Canvas-plugin-owned design with a fail-closed Activity auth model?
rationale: The unresolved blockers cross plugin ownership, Gateway authorization, token transport, and operator config shape, so automation can identify defects but should not choose the permanent Activity security boundary.

options.title: Rebuild under Canvas plugin auth
options.body: Port the work to `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require explicit Activity credentials, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and add live Discord proof before merge.

options.title: Continue through the newer PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/65205 as the working branch only after resolving its similar security, compatibility, proof, and merge-conflict blockers.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Leave Discord Activities out of core until maintainers settle the security model and whether this belongs in the Canvas plugin or an external package.

recommendation.title: Rebuild under Canvas plugin auth
recommendation.body: Port the work to `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require explicit Activity credentials, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and add live Discord proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The highest-risk decision is the Canvas plugin and Gateway auth boundary, and recent Canvas route/config history points to steipete most strongly.
